steps.what: Estimate meat requirements by counting supplies left in inventories.
Decide order quantities that maintain meat inventories for expected sales.
Write the requisition listing meat supplies and quantities to order.
Send the accepted meat requisition to the supplier.

tasks.design: She still counts the cabinet and still decides the quantities. She types item, quantity, supplier and needed date into {PROCUREMENT}. A separate send transmits only that accepted requisition.
tasks.previous_blocker: The quantity lived on a paper list, and the order was phoned or retyped later.
tasks.enabler_now: A purchasing record can send the fields she typed.
tasks.still_hard: Judging how much will sell before the next delivery still happens at the counter.
tasks.human_edge: She sees what is left in the cabinet.
tasks.altitude: She still counts the cabinet and still decides how much to order. The only shorter step is sending the requisition she already accepted.

reach.role: Meat, Poultry, and Fish Cutters and Trimmers
reach.task: portion a carcass to the counter's usual cuts
reach.learn: which cuts sell out so the requisition names those portions

evidence.claim: A purchasing or mail send can transmit the order she typed. The cabinet count and the quantity decision are not shortened. Model knowledge.

assumptions: s3 produces the requisition fields the send uses: item, quantity, supplier and needed date.
If the send cannot go, she phones the same fields she typed. That spoken order is why the low end is not the full send share.
Keeping the supplier list and item names current takes about 1 hour per 100 baseline hours.
Counting the cabinet stays hers. The machine sends only the version she accepted in s3.
The re-read before she accepts the requisition is already inside s3 and is not subtracted again.
unknowns: Whether the shop has a supplier portal or only a phone call.
research_questions: Is today's meat order a phone call, a paper list, or a portal form?

already_counted.description: She re-reads the requisition before she accepts it.

incremental.description: Supplier list and item names, reviewed a few times a year.

approvals.approved_version: requisition she accepted in s3: item, quantity, supplier and needed date

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a week the supplier only takes a phone call, so she still speaks the order. High: two standing orders the purchasing record already holds, and only the send is shorter.

tasks.short: Record meat received, issued and sold

steps.what: Check received meat on the bench before writing any record.
Draft description, quantity, supplier, lot and dispatch date from the note.

loop.output: a draft of description, quantity, supplier, lot and dispatch date
loop.check: those words mean a food description, a quantity and a lot, not only that the fields are non-empty
loop.stop: if the note is unreadable she types the lines herself

steps.what: Match description, quantity and lot to the order and the label.
File the accepted goods in lines into the stock record.
Write the quantity of meat issued to cooks.
File the accepted issue lines for meat handed to cooks.
Keep meat sales quantities beside the received and issued records.
File the accepted sales totals she kept for that day.

tasks.design: A bounded read of the paper delivery note drafts description, quantity, supplier, lot and dispatch date. She matches those words to the order and the label, and adds the beef label fields from the label in her hand. {OPS_SYSTEM} then files three separate accepted versions: the goods-in lines, the issue lines she wrote for the cooks, and the day's sales totals from the till, with no staff names.
tasks.previous_blocker: A paper register glued supplier notes to the till.
tasks.enabler_now: The till already has each sale, and a record can store the delivery fields she checked.
tasks.still_hard: Reading a smudged note and deciding a short delivery still happens at the door.
tasks.human_edge: She matches the tray to the label.
tasks.altitude: She still checks the delivery, still matches the label, and still writes what she hands the cooks. Filing the three accepted records is the part that leaves her week.

reach.role: Meat, Poultry, and Fish Cutters and Trimmers
reach.task: name the issued cuts the counter still needs
reach.learn: which issued cuts the trimmers need named on the issue line

evidence.claim: A records app can store fields she or the till already produced. The bench check, the label match and the handoff to cooks are not shortened. Model knowledge.
For food of animal origin the record is description, quantity, supplier, lot and dispatch date, updated daily, and kept until the food is assumed eaten, handed over without undue delay.
Beef labels carry a reference code, slaughterhouse and cutting plant numbers and countries of birth, rearing and slaughter.
Stock and sales records are basic records (basisgegevens), kept 7 years.

assumptions: s3 produces the accepted goods-in lines, including the beef label fields she reads from the label in her hand: reference code, slaughterhouse and cutting plant numbers, and countries of birth, rearing and slaughter.
s5 produces the issue lines: item, quantity and cook station. s7 accepts a sales snapshot of item and quantity only.
Till totals are produced by the existing till. That runtime is not her labour and is not counted as a saving.
The sales snapshot stores no staff name, so this design does not rank people on till logins.
If the note is unreadable, the draft stops and she types the lines in s3. If the till export is missing, she copies the day's totals by hand inside s7. Those exceptions are why the low end is 8.
Item names and the lot field list are reviewed a few times a year, about 1 hour per 100 baseline hours.
The re-read before she accepts goods-in is already inside s3, and the re-read of the sales snapshot is already inside s7.
unknowns: Whether sales already come off the till as a total she trusts.
Whether goods-in is still a paper register.
research_questions: Does the shop keep goods-in in a paper register, and does she already trust the till's daily item totals?
Is there a works council that would have to be asked before any staff-level till record?

already_counted.description: She matches the draft to the order and the label before she accepts the goods-in lines.
She checks the day's item totals before she accepts the sales snapshot.

incremental.description: Item names and the lot field list, reviewed a few times a year.

approvals.approved_version: goods-in lines she accepted in s3: description, quantity, supplier, lot, dispatch date and beef label fields
issue lines she wrote in s5: item, quantity and cook station
sales snapshot she accepted in s7: item and quantity sold, with no staff name

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: paper notes she still types, only the issue filing and the sales filing come off, and some days the till export fails. High: the notes are clean and the draft is usable, and she still checks every line.

steps.what: Read last prices and the quantities the shop still needs.
Negotiate order details with representatives of supply companies.
Write the agreed order details she is willing to accept.
Send the accepted order details to the supply company.

tasks.design: She still negotiates with the supplier's representative. She writes the agreed item, quantity, price and delivery day, and {EMAIL} sends only that accepted note.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agreed prices lived in a call, and a second copy was written later.
tasks.enabler_now: Mail can send the note she wrote.
tasks.still_hard: The price and the cut are still argued in the call.
tasks.human_edge: She knows what the cabinet will sell.
tasks.altitude: She still negotiates the price and the cut. Sending the note she accepted is the only shorter step.

reach.task: prepare a batch to a set weight

evidence.claim: The talk with the supplier's representative stays hers. A send only transmits the note she accepted. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The confirmation is a different note from the meat requisition: item, quantity, price and delivery day, produced in s3.
A shop that only phones once should not count both this send and the requisition send. The low end is a week she phones and does not send the note.
If mail cannot go, she reads the same note on the phone. That fallback is her time, not a second machine send.
Keeping price fields current takes about 1 hour per 100 baseline hours.
The re-read before she accepts the note is already inside s3.
unknowns: Whether the supplier takes a written confirmation or only a phone call.
research_questions: After a price talk, does she send a written note or only repeat the terms by phone?
